name: Forked beard

card.summary: A beard whose chin hair is divided into two points, worn as a distinctive grooming style that adds shape to the lower face.

quick.overview:
A forked beard is a beard style in which the chin hair is split into two points. It is listed among the beard fashions of Renaissance Europe in the sixteenth century, alongside the Spanish spade, English square cut and stiletto beards [1].

People wear it for a stylized, defined lower face and a distinctive look.
quick.how: It is grown out and shaped by trimming, with the length and split maintained by regular grooming.
quick.risks: None documented beyond ordinary grooming issues such as irritation.

lead: The forked beard is a beard style whose end is divided into two points. It is named among sixteenth-century European beard styles, when beards became fashionable again, especially after the Reformation [1]. Other styles of that era included the Spanish spade, English square cut and stiletto beards [1].

Beards have gone in and out of fashion across history, from the clean-shaven elite of the eighteenth century to the post-1848 beard revival and the full-beard fashion of the 2010s [1]. A forked beard is a stylized choice within that range.

angle.text: The style alters the outline of the lower face and is chosen for its stylized look.

paras: A general history of beards places the forked beard in the Renaissance, among styles that included the Spanish spade, English square cut and stiletto [1].

timeline.event: Forked beard named among fashionable European beard styles [1]
